The failing test `testUnionOfVariableAndNode` from `VariableTest` class creates an XML document, defines a variable "var" with value "varValue", and then iterates over pointers using the XPath expression "$var | /MAIN/A".

The current bug report indicates that an exception is thrown for the XPath "$var | /MAIN/A" with the message "Cannot compare pointers that do not belong to the same tree: '$var' and ''". This suggests that there is an issue with comparing pointers that do not belong to the same tree.

Looking at the code snippet for the test, we see that the problematic XPath expression is used in the `iteratePointers` method of the `JXPathContext` class. This method takes an XPath expression as input and returns an iterator over pointers.

The issue likely lies in how the `iteratePointers` method is handling the combination of the variable "$var" and the node "/MAIN/A" in the XPath expression. It seems that the pointers for "$var" and "/MAIN/A" are being compared in a way that assumes they belong to the same tree, leading to the exception when they are not.

To resolve this issue, the comparison logic in the `iteratePointers` method needs to be adjusted to handle pointers from different trees appropriately.

Next, I will suggest which methods should be fixed based on this diagnosis.
The issue can be fixed by adjusting the comparison logic in the `NodePointer.compareNodePointers` method which is likely used in the `JXPathContext.iteratePointers` method. 

Here are the methods to be fixed:
```
org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.NodePointer.compareNodePointers(NodePointer, NodePointer)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
